ref_speedup_note: Anchor 5.69 calibrated in oracle mode on NVIDIA H20. tests/ref_speedup.txt is authoritative at scoring; this file is only the in-image fallback. See tests/ref_speedup.caveat.md to re-measure on your hardware.
value_axis: SM occupancy / achieved throughput in the few-output/large-K regime. gpu_bench.py prints achieved-GFLOP/s per shape as work evidence; the baseline sits far below device peak because too few blocks are launched, and spreading the inner-dimension reduction across blocks lifts it.
compile_note: gemm.py JIT-compiles gemm_kernel.cu with nvcc (torch cpp-extension) at scoring; a changed .cu forces a fresh recompile. Requires nvcc + CUDA headers (cuda_runtime.h) + ninja in the image (see the Dockerfile build notes); H20 = sm_90; -ccbin g++-11 fallback. Plain float32 CUDA cores only — no fp16/tensor-core headers needed.
determinism_note: tolerance is rtol=atol=1e-3 (tighter than the fp16 sibling). The reference accumulates the long inner dimension in float64, and the intended solution combines its partial inner-dimension sums in a FIXED order (deterministic two-pass reduce, no atomics), so there is no run-to-run reassociation drift and 1e-3 holds. A candidate that combines partials with unordered atomics still passes comfortably here (only ~split small partials are summed), but an unbounded/racing reduction that drifts beyond 1e-3 would fail metamorphic/hidden parity.
